violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. Observed cheese pancakes at 82F (1.5hr) and beef cutlets at 87F (1.5hr) cooling in containers.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC placed cheese pancakes and beef cutlets on ice packs for rapid cooling to 70F.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: Observed cheese pancakes and beef cutlets cooling in containers that do not allow adequate heat transfer.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS instructed PIC on proper cooling methods, including using equipment to maximize heat transfer through the container walls.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: Observed fluorescent bulbs missing protective shields throughout the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Ensure that protective shields are installed on all fluorescent bulbs. PIC will email a technician invoice to EHS.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program

CFM CERTIFICATION IS EXPIRED AND STATES THAT SHE WILL RE-CERTIFY THIS FRIDAY. A CFM MUST BE PRESENT AT ALL TIMES DURING THE OPERATION OF THE KITCHEN. A FOLLOW WILL OCCUR TO VERIFY A VALID CFM CERTIFICATION.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours: container of cooked potatoes (44f-49f) this morning
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC DISCARDED THE COOKED POTATOES. ALLOW FOOD TO COOL STARTING FROM 57c (135f) TO 21c (70f) IN 2 HOURS OR LESS, THEN FROM 21c (70f) TO 5c (41f) FOR THE REMAINING TIME. TOTAL COOLING TIME SHOULD TAKE 6 HOURS TO COMPLETE. SEE COOLING HANDOUT.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. EHS observed food being stored directly on the floor of the walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO PURCHASE NSF APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS TO ELEVATE THE FOOD OFF OF THE FLOOR.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: Observed prepared foods being stored in plastic storage containers in the walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO BUY NSF APPROVED/ FOOD SAFE CONTAINERS. CONTAINERS CAN BE PURCHASED FROM RESTAURANT SUPPLY STORES.
